title: Dagon
lead: An old grain and storm god of Syria and Mesopotamia, worshiped by the Philistines at Ashdod and Gaza. In the Bible his statue falls before the ark (1 Samuel 5), and Samson brings down his temple (Judges 16).

sections.h: Dagon in history and in the Bible
sections.b: Dagan was worshiped along the Middle Euphrates from the third millennium BC, at Mari and Ebla, and at Ugarit, where Baal is called "son of Dagan." His name is most likely linked to the Hebrew dagan, "grain." The old idea that he was a fish god, from Hebrew dag, "fish," is found in medieval Jewish interpreters such as Radak, and most scholars now reject it. The Philistines seem to have taken him over when they settled in Canaan. Judges 16:23 tells of a feast to Dagon at Gaza, 1 Samuel 5 of his temple at Ashdod, 1 Chronicles 10:10 of Saul's head hung in a temple of Dagon, and 1 Maccabees 10:83–84 of Jonathan burning Dagon's temple at Ashdod about 147 BC. Place names such as Beth-dagon (Joshua 15:41; Joshua 19:27) show the god was known in Canaan before the Philistines.
